prompts.name: 苔轮水坊
prompts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: one standalone transparent architectural variant for the Firefly Grove underwater aquarium theme.
Input image 1 is the edit target and approved paint/material reference: Glowroot Cottage. Structurally redesign it into the requested DIFFERENT building below, preserving its exact family of painterly aged chestnut root wood, pale gray-green weathered limestone, olive/sage moss, delicate lavender bell flowers and restrained warm amber light. Keep the hand-painted Japanese fantasy environment-art finish, subtle desaturated contours, green-filtered upper-left lighting and mild frontal/right-side perspective. Do not keep the cottage's overall squat house silhouette if the requested type calls for another silhouette.
This is an independent game decoration cutout, not an illustration of a whole environment. Make the actual object solid, with real RGBA transparency outside and through any open architectural gaps. Completely remove dark/olive background matte, hazy backdrop and vignette from the reference. No cast-shadow sheet or detached glow. Full complete silhouette, all tips and feet uncut; at least 7% clean transparent margin on every side and 10% under the feet. No text, UI, fish, people, animals, frame, giant attached tree, landscape, separate ground island, companion house, contact sheet or extra asset. No pink shells, polished white palace, bright gold trim, cartoon outlines, plastic 3D, isometric city view or photorealistic render.
Only one connected building, with a short architectural stone threshold/root footing. Keep architectural structure readable at thumbnail size, fewer larger material planes instead of tiny clutter. New output only; the approved cottage is a retained separate asset.

Requested redesign: a compact ROOTWOOD WATERWHEEL WORKSHOP, approximately 1.2 times as wide as tall. Its defining silhouette is one large, complete, upright circular wooden waterwheel attached to the LEFT side of a small moss-roofed workshop on the right. The wheel has a clearly legible thick aged-wood rim, six to eight simple spokes and a few broad paddles, a restrained moss edge and an integrated stone axle support. The workshop uses one gently curved root-rib roof with a thin moss carpet, one small arched door and a single warm amber window, materially matching the reference. The wheel is architecture, not a ship steering wheel mounted on a house front. Keep all wheel paddles and roof tips inside the canvas. No river, stream, waterfall, splash, flowing water, canal, trough across the canvas, windmill blades or extra cottage. A few connected root feet join wheel and workshop into one compact asset.

Requested redesign: a slender VERTICAL FOREST LOOKOUT WITH A WARM LANTERN ROOM, about twice as tall as wide. A modest gray-green stone foot supports an elegantly tapered structure formed by two curved aged root-wood uprights. Above a small arched lower door, the open-sided upper lookout holds one warm seedpod lantern enclosed by simple wood mullions. Cap it with a compact sweeping leaf-shaped moss roof, not a stone castle spire. Two or three thin fern fronds and a sparse drape of lavender bells grow from roof edges. Give the upper lantern room a strong readable silhouette and quiet amber light, with the same hand-painted wood/moss/stone material handling as the input. No clock face, bell, industrial lighthouse beam, antenna, flags, external spiral staircase, huge tree trunk or detached elements. Keep it graceful and small-town scale, complete base-to-roof on a portrait-oriented transparent canvas.

Requested redesign: a low-wide OPEN ROOTWOOD GARDEN PAVILION, about 1.5 times as wide as tall. It must read as an OPEN shelter rather than another enclosed cottage. A single gently arched, broad moss-and-leaf roof rests on two curving root-wood side posts joined by one elegant organic arch; the center and side openings remain truly transparent so aquarium water can be seen through. Include one simple built-in wooden bench at the back, a tiny hanging warm seedpod lantern under the eave, a low gray-green stone step and a few attached lavender bell flowers. The roof profile and aged wood grain must match the approved cottage but the airy negative-space silhouette is distinct. No door, solid wall filling the opening, table service, books, furniture scattered around, people, hanging curtains, railings across the whole opening, gazebo on a floating island or attached huge tree. All posts and feet form one complete compact decoration.
